subject: SKU fingerprint, PO stamping and temporary spend lock
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.t@skylinpayments.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, procurement@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: 2026-08-30T16:12:00Z
Subject: Vendor onboarding: PO stamping & spend cap — Skyline Payments

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the quick onboarding cadence so far. I've attached our completed vendor onboarding PDF (Skyline_onboarding_form.pdf) and a preliminary SKU export. Before we go live on Redwood, procurement at Skyline needs clarity on three things that typically block our AP team:

1) PO number stamping: our billing team requires a single PO number stamped on each invoice and on the GL line so our ERP can auto-apply payments. Do you have a canonical PO issuance pattern (one-time PO vs. rolling PO per month)? Will Redwood stamp the invoice PDF you receive or do we need to submit invoices to a separate billing mailbox?

2) Spend cap / provisional hold: because this is a new vendor relationship we need a spend cap set at onboarding. Can Redwood issue a provisional PO with a temporary spend lock (we can escalate later) and show that cap in your invoice preview/portal?

3) SKU fingerprint mismatch: our finance team noticed the SKU strings in our catalog don't always match Redwood's line-item fingerprints. When Skyline invoices reference SKU-PP-497 but your ledger shows SKU-PP-497A it causes a reconciliation mismatch and our system creates a hold. We can send a corrected SKU mapping if you prefer — attaching a small CSV extract for reference.

If you can confirm the PO pattern and whether a provisional PO can be issued to hold $75k pending SKU reconciliation, we can proceed with final signatures.

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Head of Vendor Ops — Skyline Payments
elena.t@skylinpayments.com
+1 415-555-0182

Attachment: Skyline_onboarding_form.pdf (PDF)
Attachment: sku_audit_spreadsheet.csv (CSV)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Elena Torres <elena.t@skylinpayments.com>
Cc: procurement@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-30T19:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Vendor onboarding: PO stamping & spend cap — Skyline Payments

Hi Elena,

Appreciate the thorough submission and the SKU extract — that's helpful. Short answers up front: we can issue a provisional PO that gets stamped on invoices we process, and we can show a spend cap in the Console UI tied to that PO. A couple of details so we align on process:

- PO issuance model: For new vendors we typically issue a provisional, reusable PO (PO-RDW-YYYY-NNNN) that persists while the account is in onboarding. Once billing patterns stabilize we convert to a permanent PO sequence if requested. That provisional PO gets added to the invoice metadata we deliver to your ERP (we stamp the Redwood PO when we route invoices to payments).

- Temporary spend cap: We can set the provisional PO's cap to $75,000 as you requested. That will flag any invoices that attempt to post beyond the cap and trigger an internal hold. Our CS/Finance workflow can remove the hold after reconciliation.

- SKU mapping / fingerprint: Thanks for the CSV — please send a cleaned mapping with two columns (Skyline_SKU, Redwood_SKU). Our onboarding team will load that into the PO metadata so the line-item fingerprints match during invoice ingest. Until we load the mapping we recommend leaving the spending on hold.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm $75,000 provisional cap (reply-all)
2) I create PO-RDW-2026-6832 and attach provisional_po_PO-RDW-2026-6832.pdf to this thread
3) Skyline shares the cleaned SKU mapping (two-column CSV) and I'll route to procurement ops for ingestion (ticket PROC-4872)

If that sounds good I'll stand up the provisional PO today.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Manager, Procurement Ops | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Attachment: vendor_onboarding_form_filled.pdf (PDF)

From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-31T14:18:00Z
Subject: Internal: provisional PO + spend lock for Skyline (PROC-4872)

Karthik / Laura,

Following up on Elena's ask — I recommend we proceed as Karthik outlined but add two controls on our side:

1) Create provisional PO-RDW-2026-6832 with a $75,000 cap and mark the PO status as "onboarding-hold" in the ledger until SKU mapping is ingested. That prevents any automated payments but allows invoices to post to the vendor account for visibility.

2) Add a quick validation that matches incoming invoice SKU strings against the mapping; if >10% of line items mismatch, auto-flag the invoice and notify both Redwood accounting and Skyline contacts.

I created a Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PROC-4872 to track loading the mapping and the validation rule. I'll attach the provisional PO PDF to the Jira and to the vendor thread. Once Skyline confirms the corrected CSV we can close the ticket and flip the PO to an active state.

Priyom Das
Procurement Systems | Redwood Inference
Attachment: provisional_po_PO-RDW-2026-6832.pdf (PDF)

From: Elena Torres <elena.t@skylinpayments.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-01T15:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Vendor onboarding: PO stamping & spend cap — Skyline Payments

Karthik / Priyom,

Thanks — we confirm the $75,000 provisional spend cap and accept PO-RDW-2026-6832 as the provisional PO. Attached is a cleaned SKU mapping CSV (sku_audit_spreadsheet.csv) with columns Skyline_SKU, Redwood_SKU — we removed legacy suffixes and normalized the fingerprint.

Please let us know when the mapping is ingested so we can request the hold be released; we expect to submit two invoices this week and would like them processed against the provisional PO.

I'll also route a signed copy of our MSA via DocuSign once procurement confirms the final terms.

Best,
Elena
Attachment: sku_audit_spreadsheet.csv (CSV)
